newsitem.title: UK: Egypt's Kato to buy stake in Koor - paper. [CORRECTED 08:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Egypt's Kato to buy stake in Koor - paper. [CORRECTED 08:55 GMT]

text.p: Egypt's Kato Industries plans to buy a substantial stake in Israel's Koor Industries Ltd this month, forming a strategic link in support of Middle East peace efforts, the Financial Times reported on Wednesday.
Mansour El-Tarzi, financial adviser to Kato chairman Ibrahim Kamel, was quoted by the newspaper as saying the Koor shares would be purchased on January 28 or 29.
"It's not primarily a commercial transaction. It's to send a signal, to make a gesture that has meaning," El-Tarzi said.
The report did not say how many shares Kato planned to buy. (Corrects to delete reference to Kato as being "Cairo-listed" - it is a privately-held company).
Kamel met Koor's chief executive Benjamin Gaon earlier this month during a visit to Israel. The Kato chairman said he did not plan to sign any deals during the 24-hour stay.
Kato's interests range from trade and banking to insurance and aviation, while Koor's businesses centre on building materials, chemicals and telecommunications.
